tickets.title: Catalogue loads that do not fail at random, and run faster (**amendment 13, E25, 2026-10-28**)

authority.locator: E25 · section 2 of amendment 13, "Done when" (lane L20's finding, R-P540; the diagnosis S42/analyst-503, R-P543; in force by section 3 row 1, R-P544)
authority.requirement: a failed storage call on the load's path is retried once inside the request (bounded, idempotent: exact-creates and reads only); the load's calls run in a bounded pool without batch barriers; the 503 names the operation, the object kind and the storage error's number (never a key or a body) and a `state` — `nothing_written`, `pending` (recover) or `committed`; the `changed` count compares records independent of field order; the purge collects the objects a refused load left once they are older than the grace; kit 02 and kit 03 state the load protocol (file size, client timeout, read the status then recover or re-send); the live walk measures the refusal rate and the time per 5,000 products on both pair hosts, one host at a time.

tickets.outcome: A catalogue load of the size the customer sends is accepted in storage calls bounded by the index shards it touches and in a bounded time, is never refused for one transient storage failure, answers an exact changed count, says on any refusal what failed and what state it left, and leaves nothing behind that the purge does not collect, while a product page's reads stay bounded.

criteria.observable: A load's storage calls are bounded by the shards it touches, not by its product count, to the target the lead's redesign ruling names (its number is entered in this criterion when the lead amends this work order before the specification). Today a load makes one exact-create per changed product's part (src/routes/content.ts:263–266; src/config/publication.ts:658–668, :611–614), one read per touched product shard and per touched id shard, awaited one product and one id at a time (content.ts:303–320 through :1468–1471 and :1478–1486), and one exact-create per moved shard (content.ts:376–379; publication.ts:832–844): 468 calls for 100 products, 2,018 for 1,000 and 6,044 for 5,000 at 40,000 products (S42/analyst-503/DIAGNOSIS.md §1, REPRODUCED), the writes eight at a time with a barrier after each eight (content.ts:265, :378), so a 5,000-product load is about 1,250 sequential steps (546 reads and 702 write rounds, §2).
criteria.proof: The P98 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P98.LD1 in src/units/P98/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: A 40,000-product file loads within the time the lead's ruling names (entered with LD1's number), on both hosts in the harness with every storage call held a fixed delay, and no load is refused for one transient storage failure: a failed idempotent call on the load's path (a read; an exact-create of content-addressed bytes, where a precondition failure on identical bytes counts as success as today, publication.ts:611–614) is retried inside the request, and the head's compare-and-set (publication.ts:987) and the commit (:905) are never re-sent blindly (a lost race answers 409 as today). Today nothing is retried (grep -n -i "retry\|setTimeout\|timeout" src/config/publication.ts finds comment lines only: :625, :656, :721, :831, :1014), one failed call refuses the whole load (lane L20: 29 of 193 fill loads refused 503, fitting about 1 failed call in 8,000; R-P540, R-P543), a 5,000-product file took about 200 s live, and one file is capped at 10,000 records and 2 MiB of input (INPUT_MAX_RECORDS and INPUT_MAX_BYTES, src/config/input.ts:2–3, applied at src/content/import.ts:203, :232, :243, :307), so a 40,000-product file is refused 413 input_budget_exceeded before the load starts; src/config/input.ts and src/content/import.ts are outside this grant, which the ruling settles.
criteria.proof: The P98 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P98.LD2 in src/units/P98/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: A product page's reads and bytes stay within the bound the lead's ruling names (entered with LD1's number) at any catalogue size, on both hosts. Today the anchor's page reads the head, the set, the four revisions, the anchor's product shard and its part, 8 reads cold and the head alone warm (P93 CS2; R-P506), through src/content/service.ts:1436–1443 and src/config/publication.ts:889–898 (the shard, :851–861; the part, :674–684); the manifest is 55,939 bytes live at 40,000 products (R-P540) and the largest shard 20,112 bytes in the harness at 40,000 (R-P506).
criteria.proof: The P98 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P98.LD3 in src/units/P98/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: The 503 a load's storage failure answers names its cause and the state it left: the operation, the object's kind, the storage error's status where known, and state, one of nothing_written, pending (recover with POST /content/catalog/publication/recover) and committed, matching the store in each of the diagnosis's scenarios (S42/analyst-503/DIAGNOSIS.md §1: rows 1 to 6a nothing written, rows 6c to 8 the head pending, row 8 after the commit and row 10 committed), and never an object key, a body or a token. Today every storage failure is one answer: storageFailure and required (src/config/publication.ts:79–84) throw unavailable() (:49–50) from every read (:190), every put (:609) and every malformed storage answer, and contentRoutes.onError answers { ok: false, error, code } with no cause and no state (src/routes/content.ts:67), although the publication's own status already tells pending from committed (publicationStatus, publication.ts:1048–1065). LOCK: the absent-member refusals keep their bodies byte for byte (absent, publication.ts:57–63; src/units/P54/LEDGER.unit.test.ts:258–268).
criteria.proof: The P98 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P98.LD4 in src/units/P98/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: The changed count is exact: on both hosts a one-product retitle answers changed equal to the records it changed, on a fresh isolate and on a warm one, in the committed answer and in the dry run. Today changedPieces compares JSON.stringify strings (src/routes/content.ts:1013–1018) of the stored part, read back in canonical key order (src/config/publication.ts:88–93, :674–684) or held in the validator's order by the isolate that wrote it (:665), against the validator's output (content.ts:1522–1551), so a cold isolate counts every record of the product (live: changed 1199 for one retitle, R-P540; harness: 5 of 5 cold and 1 warm, S42/analyst-503/DIAGNOSIS.md §4); the answers at content.ts:1663 and :1676 carry it.
criteria.proof: The P98 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P98.LD5 in src/units/P98/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: A refused load leaves nothing the purge does not collect: the parts, product shards and id shards a refused load stored are removed by the purge once older than the 15-minute grace (ATTACHMENT_GRACE_MS, src/config/publication.ts:1439), and the purge never removes an object that the revision in force, a pending publication or any other stored revision names (P93 CS5's rule, LOCK), nor one that a load in flight has adopted by its exact-create before that load's head reservation settles (an exact-create that finds identical bytes keeps the stored object and its old upload time, publication.ts:611–614, :1441–1447, and the kit's re-send of the same file adopts what the refused attempt stored). Today the purge reaches only the objects a purged revision named (orphansOf, publication.ts:1376–1411) and lists only their directories (sweep, :1420–1437), so an object no revision ever named is never collected (187 objects survived 12 publications, S42/analyst-503/DIAGNOSIS.md §4); the purge runs only after a publication under the tenant's configuration-revision setting (publication.ts:991, :1300–1305).
criteria.proof: The P98 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P98.LD6 in src/units/P98/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: Kits 02 and 03 state the load as built: the file size and the time a load takes, the client timeout, what the 503 of a storage failure names and how to act on each state (read GET /content/catalog/publication, recover if pending, else re-send with fresh preconditions), the exact changed count and the collection of a refused load's objects. Today kit 03 :387–392 advises files of about 200 to 300 products and calls the platform's per-request limit not yet measured (lane L20 met no size refusal up to 5,000 products, R-P540), kit 02 :1831 (the import row) names no storage refusal and :1844 says only that unavailable, corrupt or unconfirmed storage answers 503, and neither kit names publication_unavailable (grep -n publication_unavailable docs/kit/02-api-reference.md docs/kit/03-payload-schemas.md: no line).

tickets.title: The purge at scale (**amendment 13, E23, 2026-10-28**)

authority.locator: E23 · section 2 of amendment 13, "Done when" (P93's delivery review, R-P506; P95's delivery review, R-P531; in force by section 3 row 1, R-P544)
authority.requirement: the purge keeps its progress across passes so a large revision is removed over several publications; the latent delete order (shard keys queued before the parts behind them) cannot strand a part; a tenant whose salt count can never be established is told (an advisory on the operator's reads) and its learn revisions purged past a stated bound once the count is null for good, or the owner's alternative.

tickets.outcome: The purge removes every revision past the tenant's setting however large its load was, without stranding a part, and a tenant whose salt count can never be established is told so and does not keep every learn revision for good.

criteria.observable: On both hosts, a tenant under the configuration-revision setting whose catalogue holds 40,000 products and whose stored revisions include loads that each touched all 256 product shards and 256 id shards (eight 5,000-product loads, as P93's delivery review loaded them): once those revisions are past the setting, each is removed, its body and the shards and parts only it names, over a bounded number of later publications, each publication's purge within its own budget (PURGE_OPERATIONS 256 and PURGE_BYTES, src/config/publication.ts:1273–1274, :1281) and its progress kept from one publication to the next; nothing another stored revision names is removed and nothing is left that no stored revision names. Today each publication's purge starts afresh: orphansOf reads every shard a revision names, one budget call each (publication.ts:1376–1386), before sweep lists or deletes anything (:1420–1437), so a revision naming 512 shards exhausts the budget on every pass and is never removed (R-P506 (2): eight such revisions never purged across 20 publications; S37/reviewer-p93/REPORT-e20cefda.md:51).
criteria.proof: The P99 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P99.PG1 in src/units/P99/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: No order of deletions can strand a part: the purge deletes the parts a shard names before that shard, or both in one deletion call, so a purge that stops at any call (its budget, PurgeStopped at src/config/publication.ts:1281, or a failed deletion) leaves every part it has not deleted reachable by the next pass through a stored shard or a stored revision; shown with the purge stopped after each deletion call in turn. Today orphansOf queues a shard's key (publication.ts:1402) before the parts behind it (:1404), sweep groups the keys by directory in that order (:1421–1422) and deletes them 1,000 to a call (:1436), so a stop between the shard directory's call and the part directory's leaves parts whose shard is gone, which the next pass no longer reaches (the shard read answers null, :1381–1383) (R-P506 (3), latent under today's budget; S37/reviewer-p93/REPORT-e20cefda.md:52).
criteria.proof: The P99 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P99.PG2 in src/units/P99/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: On both hosts, a tenant whose salt count can never be established is told and does not keep every learn revision for good: where its stored learn history cannot establish the count, because a learn revision before the current one was purged (410 revision_purged, src/config/publication.ts:597–598) or the history starts at a retained baseline (minRevision above 1, :1135; the count refused 409 legacy_history_unavailable at :591), the operator's learn reads (GET /content/learn and the success answers of PUT /content/learn and POST /content/learn/validate, through the learn advisory channel, src/routes/content.ts:953–970, :1195, :1279, :1404) carry an advisory naming the unknown salt version and why, and under the configuration-revision setting the purge removes that tenant's learn revisions past a bound that is a code constant and that kit 02 states, under the purge's other rules (older than the setting, neither the current nor the previous revision, named by no stored replay manifest; publication.ts:1223–1238). A count that could not finish for a transient storage failure is not one that can never be established: every learn revision is kept until a publication establishes it, as today (P95 SV2 and SV4, LOCK), and a purge never turns an exact count into an unknown (W38 B4, LOCK). Today saltCountCarried answers no for every null count (publication.ts:1471–1475; saltVersionOf answers null for any unfinished count, src/content/holdout.ts:117, :121), so such a tenant keeps every learn revision for good under the setting and is told nothing (R-P531 (2); S39/reviewer-p95/REPORT-44f9bbc4.md:69–70, :86); kit 02 :1844 says the purge keeps every learn revision where the current one carries no exact count.
criteria.proof: The P99 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P99.PG3 in src/units/P99/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision, and the reviewer reads the changed sentences at that revision.

criteria.observable: On the pair's next release (lane L21; the stamps read-only), on a pair tenant that sets the configuration-revision setting, a revision written by a 5,000-product load and past the setting is removed over later publications, read in GET /content/catalog/history and as 410 revision_purged on its read; whether l3 sets that setting is UNVERIFIED (S42/analyst-503/DIAGNOSIS.md, UNVERIFIED list), and where no pair tenant sets it or the lane holds no authority to publish there, the row is proxied to the PG1 and PG2 unit legs and the record says so; PG3 is proxied to its unit leg unless a pair tenant reads a salt version null for good (l1 reads an exact count, R-P540, R-P542).

tickets.title: A browser that drew while the salt version was unknown (**amendment 13, E24, 2026-10-28**)

authority.locator: E24 · section 2 of amendment 13, "Done when" (P95's delivery review, R-P531 (1); in force by section 3 row 1, R-P544)

authority.locator: E26 · section 2 of amendment 13, "Done when" (the 401 diagnosis, R-P541; in force by section 3 row 1, R-P544)
authority.requirement: the decision routes refuse a malformed `pageInstance` with `400 Invalid page instance` before any work, as they do a malformed `arm`; kit 02 states the format.

tickets.outcome: A decision request whose page-view id is malformed is refused at once as the request error it is, 400 Invalid page instance, on every decision path, and a valid id is answered as today.

criteria.observable: On both hosts, a decision request whose pageInstance is outside 1–128 characters of A-Za-z0-9_- (the empty string, a space, a comma, a slash, or 129 characters) answers 400 { ok: false, error: 'Invalid page instance' } before any work: on GET /v1/{tenant}/decisions/snapshot (the query's pageInstance) and on its POST with a session, nothing decided, nothing captured to the ledger or the ring and no render offer minted; at the first-request door (a POST with no session), before a session is issued or a shopper object created, with Cache-Control no-store as the door answers a malformed arm (src/routes/decisions.ts:1132). Today snapshotContext admits any string up to 128 characters on POST (decisions.ts:1021–1024) and any value on GET (:987–1001), the route decides (:1294) with the id as the offer (:1312), and only the render offer's mint refuses it (src/content/renderOffer.ts:62, by isEventNonce, src/events/actionTypes.ts:45–46), answered 401 Shopper session unavailable (src/identity/sessionAuthority.ts:766–767) after the decision's work, for a shopper with tracking consent on a page with a rendered-v1 slot (src/content/service.ts:1230–1234); the door answers a spaced id 200 with no offer, and its catch answers every other snapshotContext failure 401 (decisions.ts:1130–1133) (S42/analyst-401/DIAGNOSIS.md §1).
